selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What big truth does the traveller learn from the universe in this passage?
questions.answer: He learns that all creation points to Allah as the only true God and shows His oneness.

questions.question: What does the passage say about anything besides Allah?
questions.answer: Everything else is dependent and not necessary by itself.

questions.question: How many stages of indirect learning are mentioned?
questions.answer: Eighteen stages are mentioned.

questions.question: Which three ideas about the world are mentioned as signs that point to Allah?
questions.answer: Its being created, its constant changing, and its dependent nature.

questions.question: Why are change and renewal in the world important in this passage?
questions.answer: They are signs that the world is managed on purpose and is not independent.

questions.question: What does the word meaning “You alone” change in the style of speaking?
questions.answer: It changes the speech into direct address to Allah.

questions.question: What change happens when the word meaning “You alone” is reached in the opening sura?
questions.answer: The speech changes from talking about Allah to speaking directly to Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say one should ask instead of only searching from far away?
questions.answer: One should ask the One being sought.

questions.question: In the same way, what helps us know Allah?
questions.answer: His Beautiful Names and Sacred Attributes help us know Him.

questions.question: Who is the main human figure in the passage?
questions.answer: A passionate and curious traveller looking for the Creator.

questions.question: Why is the universe compared to a city and a palace?
questions.answer: Because it is arranged, full of parts, and run in an orderly way.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the rest of creation compared with Allah?
questions.answer: The rest of creation is dependent and needs Him.

questions.question: What part of the opening sura is described as praise said in an indirect way?
questions.answer: The part from the beginning until the word that means “You alone.”

questions.question: How had the traveller mostly known Allah before this point?
questions.answer: He had known Allah indirectly through what he learned from creation.

questions.question: What other features among beings are named as signs?
questions.answer: Working together, responding to one another, helping one another, balance, and preservation.

questions.question: What does the sun teach in this comparison?
questions.answer: The source of light can be known through the light it gives.

questions.question: Why is the sun a helpful example in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it shows how a source can be known through what comes from it.

questions.question: What is the shortest statement of belief taught in the first paragraph?
questions.answer: Allah alone is God, and He has no equal.

questions.question: What had he used to learn before speaking directly?
questions.answer: He had learned by looking at signs and proofs in creation.

questions.question: What kinds of parts of the universe are said to agree together in giving testimony?
questions.answer: Its foundations, kinds, pieces, tiny parts, living things, contents, and all that comes in and goes out.

questions.question: What do these pictures of the universe help the reader understand?
questions.answer: They help the reader understand that the universe has order, meaning, and a Maker.

questions.question: How is the earlier part of the opening sura described?
questions.answer: It is described as praise said without direct address.

questions.question: Why does the traveller speak to his own soul?
questions.answer: He is reminding himself to turn from only indirect searching to directly addressing Allah.

questions.question: What do the rays help us know?
questions.answer: They help us recognize the sun.
